Multi-Stage Calculation & Reverse Gross-Up Methodology

Stage 1 (Platform Deduction): After_Platform = Gross × (1 - Platform_Pct) - Platform_Fixed. Stage 2 (Payout Rail & FX Uncertainty Band): Net_USD = After_Platform × (1 - Rail_Pct - FX_Spread_[Min..Max]) - Rail_Fixed - Intermediary_[Min..Max]. Stage 3 (Gross Turnover Tax Base — e.g. RA Tax Code Art. 257): Turnover_Tax = Gross × Local_Tax_Pct; Final_Net = Net_USD - Turnover_Tax. Multi-Stage Reverse Invoice Solver: Required_Gross = (Target_Net + Platform_Fixed × (1 - Rail_Pct - FX_Spread) + Rail_Fixed + Intermediary) / ((1 - Platform_Pct) × (1 - Rail_Pct - FX_Spread) - Local_Tax_Pct).

Reference Notes & FAQ

Why is turnover tax calculated on the Gross Invoice rather than the post-fee payout?

Under gross turnover tax regimes—such as Article 257 of Armenia's Tax Code or Georgia's Small Business Status—the tax base is your gross sales revenue (the full invoice amount billed to the client), without deducting marketplace commissions (like Upwork's 10%) or bank withdrawal fees. Subtracting tax only from the remaining post-fee payout understates your legal tax obligation.

Who qualifies for Armenia's 1% High-Tech rate or 0% Micro-Business regime?

Both regimes have strict statutory eligibility requirements under the RA Tax Code. The 1% turnover tax rate applies only to qualifying high-tech/IT activities and eligible taxpayers (within the 115M AMD annual threshold), and the 0% micro-business regime (under 24M AMD) excludes several professional, consulting, and specialized service categories. Always confirm your activity classification with a certified accountant.

Does this calculator invent live exchange rates?

Never. Exchange rates fluctuate every minute and banks apply custom spreads. We provide a user-editable Reference Exchange Rate field and calculate transparent Best-Case to Worst-Case Net Payout ranges so you can see the exact impact of FX markups and SWIFT intermediary fees.
